history.summary: Identity note: this row is mapped to the famous Keladi Rameshwara Temple near Sagara, Shivamogga district (CSV town 'Shimoga' corrected to Keladi, ~8 km from Sagara). Ambiguity flagged: Shivamogga district also has a 12th-century Hoysala Rameshwara Temple at Koodli (next to CSV row 470's Narasimha temple); if the CSV intended Koodli's Rameshwara, the town should read Koodli and the id needs disambiguation. Keladi is the likelier referent because it is the district's best-known 'Rameshwara Temple'. Built c. 1499/1500 CE by Chowdappa (Chavuda/Chavadappa) Nayaka, founder of the Keladi Nayaka line - legend says he found a linga in an anthill over which his cow shed milk, and built the temple around it. The ASI-protected complex is a double temple of Rameshwara and Virabhadra with a Parvati shrine, in mixed Hoysala-Dravida (Kadamba-Vijayanagara influence) style; highlights include intricately carved stone pillars, the wooden (sandalwood-type) ceiling carvings of the Parvati shrine, the Gandabherunda (twin-headed bird) ceiling motif, a 24-ft pillar depicting Ganesh with queen Rani Chennamma, and a secret passage to the Veerabhadra shrine. Keladi was the first capital of the Keladi Nayaka kingdom. Timings conflict across listings (8 AM-6 PM per ASI-based sources vs until 7:30 PM on Justdial); verify locally. No documented festival calendar found.

name: Keladi Rameshwara Temple
town_description: Keladi is a temple village in Sagar taluk, Shivamogga district, about 8 km from Sagara town. It was the first capital of the Keladi Nayaka kingdom (founded c. 1500 CE) and is known for the Rameshwara-Veerabhadra-Parvati temple complex maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.
